newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 182nd JGB yield rises 10 bps to 2.570 pct.
newsitem.headline: Key 182nd JGB yield rises 10 bps to 2.570 pct.

text.p: The yield of the benchmark 182nd Japanese government bond rose 10 basis points to 2.570 percent in late afternoon trade on Wednesday after the Bank of Japan deputy governor was quoted as saying that BOJ is considering the right timing to raise its official discount rate.

BOJ deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying on Wednesday that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but that it does not want to make a hasty decision.

Fukui made the remark at a meeting with executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (Rengo), at which the labour group urged the BOJ to raise the discount rate, now at a record low 0.5 percent.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.590 percent as of 0607 GMT, up sharply from the previous day's close of 2.470 percent. It earlier rose as high as 2.605 percent.
